slides.title: Working with Query Strings 🔍
slides.content:
# Reading Query Parameters

Query strings like `/api/search?term=nextjs` are automatically parsed into `req.query`.

```js
// URL: /api/search?term=nextjs&limit=10
console.log(req.query); // { term: 'nextjs', limit: '10' }
```

No extra parsing needed – Next.js uses the same URL parsing as pages.

**Note:** `req.query` is an object with values always as strings or arrays of strings.

quizData.question: What type is `req.query.page` if the URL is `/api/posts?page=2`?
quizData.explanation: All query parameters are received as strings. Convert to numbers if needed.

quizData.question: Why isn't `req.body` directly available like in Express?

options.text: Because Next.js keeps the API surface minimal and doesn't include built‑in middleware
Because `req` is a browser Request object
You need to install a special package to use POST

quizData.explanation: Next.js provides the raw Node.js request object. You can parse the body manually or use a library like `micro`.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content: Use the `next-connect` library to add Express‑like middleware (`req.body`, cors) to your API routes. It makes the code cleaner for complex cases.
